question: The reduced-osmolarity ORS recommended by WHO for acute diarrhoea in children has an osmolarity of 245 mOsm/L.

l10n.wrongAnswerMessage: This statement is true. The WHO-recommended reduced-osmolarity ORS has an osmolarity of 245 mOsm/L. The original high-osmolarity ORS (311 mOsm/L) was replaced because the reduced-osmolarity formulation causes less nausea, less vomiting, and fewer unscheduled IV infusions in clinical trials.
l10n.correctAnswerMessage: Correct. Reduced-osmolarity ORS (245 mOsm/L) replaced the original 311 mOsm/L formula. It contains Na 75 mEq/L, Cl 65 mEq/L, K 20 mEq/L, citrate 10 mEq/L, and glucose 75 mmol/L. Its lower osmolarity reduces stool output and the need for IV therapy in acute diarrhoea.
